title: Design Add And Search Words Data Structure
description:
Design a class `WordDictionary`.

- `addWord(word)` stores a word made of lowercase letters.
- `search(word)` returns `true` if any stored word matches the pattern. The pattern may contain the wildcard `.`, which stands for **exactly one** arbitrary letter. The whole word must match, so lengths must agree.

examples.input: addWord("day"), addWord("bay"), addWord("may"), search("say"), search("day"), search(".ay"), search("b..")
examples.output: null, null, null, false, true, true, true

constraints: Added words contain lowercase letters only
Search patterns contain lowercase letters or '.'

complexity.time: addWord O(L); search O(L) without dots, up to O(26^d * L) worst case with d dots

hints: A plain set answers dot-free searches, but wildcards break hashing. A trie keeps words organised by position.
Walk the trie letter by letter. For a normal letter follow one child; for '.' you have to consider every child.
Write search recursively as search(index, node): at '.' return true if any child works; the pattern matches only if you finish on a node marked as a word end.

solution.explanation: Store words in a trie of dict nodes with an end marker. addWord is the ordinary trie insert. search runs a DFS over (position, node): a normal letter follows its single child, while '.' tries every child and succeeds if any branch matches. A pattern matches only when the last character lands on a node flagged as a word end. Adding costs O(L); searching costs O(L) with no dots and only branches at dots, so at most a few dots keeps it cheap.
